summary: Observations of a luminous disk in the sky that seems to follow the observers: observations of the Moon.
description: On November 12, 1986, starting at 2:45 a.m., several people in Vendin-Le-Viel (62) and Henin-Beaumont (62) observed a luminous phenomenon in the sky that intrigued them. This observation of a luminous disk that seemed to follow the observers is of a type now well known to ufologists: a misidentification of a celestial body, the Moon in this case. It is noted that this was the initial interpretation of one of the witnesses: "My colleague told me: 'The Moon is very low today.'" A relevant interpretation, but one that was contested by his colleague: "So I told him: 'No, it's not the Moon.'" To verify this Moon hypothesis, it is necessary to ensure that the direction of observation is consistent with the Moon's actual position in the sky. The direction indicated by the witnesses is rather poorly described in the interview report because the witnesses do not specify which side of the road they were observing from; However, a precise piece of information is noted: "Axis of the road from Henin-Beaumont to Sallaumines," meaning due west (azimuth 270°). The star chart shows the Moon at 261° at 2:45 AM, with an elevation of 3.30°, meaning very close to the described observation axis. It is also noted later in the testimony that the witnesses did not recognize the Moon, even though it was clearly visible: "We have to be honest: there was no moon." The witnesses' drawings correspond perfectly to the Moon, gibbous that evening, temporarily and partially obscured by clouds. The description of the phenomenon's slow descent, descending obliquely, is entirely consistent with a moonset. The witness reported the disappearance at 3:07 AM, while the moon set at 3:11 AM (center of the moon on the horizon, in completely clear terrain), which is perfectly consistent. This typical case of mistaken identity—the moon observed from a car—is classified as "A," meaning it has been thoroughly identified.

summary: Flying object at an altitude of 200 meters.
description: On October 20, 1986, at approximately 8:00 PM, a witness walking in the street observed a rectangular flying object. The front of the object was rounded with a white light, and the rear ended in a triangle. Beneath the gray, metallic craft, the witness saw a red light and two green lights. The object moved slowly and silently at an altitude of approximately 200 meters. No further information was gathered.

summary: A flying object at an altitude of 600 meters at very high speed.
description: On October 6, 1986, at approximately 7:45 PM, two witnesses observed a flying object moving at very high speed and without noise. This triangular object moved from east to west at an estimated altitude of 600 meters. No further information was gathered.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of about ten green lights in the sky: observation of a bolide.
description: On February 23, 2008, GEIPAN received an email from a witness reporting an observation of a UFO on September 15, 1986, from the town of Vélizy-Villacoublay (78). Walking to work at 7:30 a.m., the witness was surprised to see about ten identical green lights moving silently from east to west in the sky. Only one witness account was recorded. Let's review the key points of the witness's description of the UFO: green color; horizontal movement from east to west; absence of noise; the presence of about ten identical lights; and the synchronized movement of all these lights. All these points suggest either an atmospheric reentry or a fragmented fireball (see the investigation report). A search of existing databases and the internet for the date and time of the observation yielded no results regarding either hypothesis. However, by broadening the search timeframe, we found other accounts of identical observations made in Germany, France, and the Benelux countries, around 7:30 a.m., but on September 23, 1986, and not September 15, 1986. In the Paris region, the press reported on these observations the very next day. The newspaper Libération, in its September 24, 1986 edition, for example, mentioned the presence of about fifteen bright points observed in the region. After investigation by several atmospheric reentry specialists and astronomers, it turned out that the phenomenon was a fragmented bolide. All its characteristics match the witness's description: color, horizontal movement from East to West, composition of about ten fragments... This testimony was given 22 years after the observation. There is every reason to believe that the witness made a mistake with the date, but the time of 7:30 AM was indeed remembered. This error is fully supported by the fact that the witness mentions the press release following the observation of September 23rd. He told me that this very morning, while driving to work, he had heard a journalist on the radio who claimed to have seen something unusual in the sky over the Île-de-France region. In conclusion, the witness observed a fragmented fireball entering the atmosphere. GEIPAN classifies the case as A: observation of a fireball.

summary: Observation of a luminous, round-shaped object moving at the speed of an airplane.
description: On September 26, 1986, at approximately 9:30 PM, a couple observed a very bright sphere for about four minutes. This sphere, roughly the size of a pétanque ball, moved from east to west at the speed of an airplane. After emitting reddish emissions, it disappeared abruptly. Despite the relatively long observation period, this sighting exhibits the characteristics of an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Long observation of bright points crossing the sky from North to South; no date of the day: lack of information.
description: This recent testimony, received in 2014, of an earlier observation (1986) does not mention a precise date (the date of August 1st is given arbitrarily). The account of bright points crossing the sky from North to South in 12 minutes in the evening clearly evokes the passage of artificial satellites, such as could be easily observed at that time and even more so today. While the zigzag trajectory described by the witness does not fit this hypothesis, the autokinetic illusion (see The perception of the movement of a bright point in the sky) explains this impression, quite frequently described by witnesses under certain observation conditions. The impression of high-speed flight corresponds to the satellite entering the Earth's shadow. As the witness did not provide a precise date, GEIPAN was unable to verify which satellite might have passed at that time. This case therefore remains in category "C" due to a lack of a precise date.

summary: Quick observation in the sky of three motionless and silent balls or discs, bright and luminous yellow in color: lack of information.
description: On July 28, 1986, at approximately 10:00 PM, two people driving towards Cazals observed three motionless and silent spheres or discs of bright, luminous yellow in the clear sky for about ten seconds. Deciding to turn back, the witnesses saw nothing further in the sky. Only one person gave a brief statement. This 1986 case was reported to GEIPAN in 2012. No simple explanation for this phenomenon has been found. An investigation into this type of case after more than 25 years is, of course, difficult to undertake. GEIPAN cannot comment: this case is classified as "C" due to a lack of information.

summary: Circle of hardened brown earth that does not absorb water.
description: On December 7, 1986, a person came forward to report the presence of a hardened earth circle in a chicken coop. This circle, 1.10 meters in diameter, had appeared sometime in June. Within a 0.40-meter ring, the earth did not absorb water, and vegetation was virtually nonexistent. Furthermore, a tingling sensation was felt when entering the circle. Two other witnesses who had seen a column of intense white light sometime in June were also interviewed as part of the investigation. The phenomenon resembled what are known as fairy rings, likely composed of mycelium that prevents any vegetation from growing. This hypothesis, however, did not explain the tingling sensation felt by the witnesses, which, moreover, could not be corroborated by any other evidence.

On April 17, 1986, at approximately 9:30 PM, a couple observed a luminous phenomenon from their apartment. A stationary red sphere, about the size of a lamppost, was observed for 15 minutes. No further information was gathered about this phenomenon.

summary: Observation of a delta wing shape: lack of information.
description: On April 15, 1986, a witness observed a silent object shaped like a delta wing from his bedroom for 30 to 40 seconds. No further information has allowed for a serious analysis of this observation.

summary: Observation of a spherical shape over 100 meters in diameter.
description: On March 22, 1986, at approximately 6:15 a.m., a witness driving his vehicle observed a spherical object moving from east to west for 7 to 8 seconds. The object was blue at the front and blue-green towards the rear. The witness estimated the object's length at 100 meters. No further information was gathered regarding this observation, which exhibited all the characteristics of an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation of a sphere illuminating the ground over an area of approximately 1000 m².
description: On March 17, 1986, at approximately 4:00 AM, a witness reported seeing a luminous phenomenon. It was a sphere emitting light. This sphere moved slowly, illuminating an area of 1,000 square meters. The observation lasted approximately 20 seconds. No further information was gathered about this phenomenon due to the very early hour.

summary: A block of blue ice falling onto the hood of a car: a block of ice from an airplane latrine effluent falling.
description: On March 1, 1986, at approximately 7:30 p.m., a witness heard a strange banging noise outside. He found the hood of his car damaged by a melting object. The witness placed the object in his refrigerator before calling the police. This blue crystalline mass smelled of detergent. Due to the force of the impact, fragments of the object were scattered in the yard, leaving blue marks on the leaves of the plants it touched. Analysis revealed that the substance was aircraft waste.

summary: Observation of a large fireball with black smoke.
description: On January 3, 1986, at dusk, a couple observed from their vehicle a large sphere that gradually and slowly descended toward the horizon. Black smoke emanated from this orange sphere. This observation lasted between two and three minutes without the object changing direction. No further information was gathered about this phenomenon.
